Definition: of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first: --Alpha. Often used (usually ἄν, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from G427) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of G260).
BiblicalUsage: Alpha is simply the first letter of the Greek alphabet, and it shows up in the New Testament only as a title for Christ. In Revelation He calls Himself the Alpha and the Omega — the beginning and the end — in the letters to the churches, in the vision of the new heaven and earth, and in the closing promise of His return.
TheologicalSignificance: The letter itself is only a letter, and the weight is not in the alphabet but in the title Christ takes from it — the beginning and the end.
